horizon_driver: annual treaty renewal cycle (1 April / 1 June / 1 July) plus quarterly solvency reporting under Solvency II / Swiss Solvency Test; multi-year catastrophe-bond and retro programmes exist but pricing power resets yearly

capabilities.note: maintain current war-risk zone list and premium schedule
re-enter/extend cover for a contested corridor, e.g. facility-backed cover like the Ukraine 'Unity' scheme
declare a zone uninsurable / withdraw war-risk cover — slow and costly to reverse once a market exits, since underwriting capacity and broker relationships take renewal cycles to rebuild

constraints.source: Net-Zero Insurance Alliance collapsed Mar-Apr 2023 after Munich Re, Zurich, Hannover Re and Swiss Re exited citing 'material antitrust risks' (Norton Rose Fulbright advice) — https://www.cadwalader.com/cwt-climate/index.php?eid=216&nid=50
constraints.breaks_under: explicit antitrust safe-harbour from regulators for coordinated underwriting exclusions — has not occurred

constraints.source: insurers collectively still earn ~$21.25bn/yr underwriting coal, oil and gas; only Aviva, Generali, Allianz, Hannover Re, Munich Re and Talanx have stopped new oil & gas extraction cover 'without major exceptions' — https://www.energymonitor.ai/finance/risk-management/insurers-double-down-on-fossil-fuel-projects-despite-record-climate-disaster-payouts/
constraints.breaks_under: profit opportunity in a hardening fossil-asset market, or reputational cost of continuing exceeds the premium earned

constraints.source: 2026 treaty renewals saw ~5% average price declines across Munich Re/Swiss Re/Hannover Re despite the Iran war, because nat-cat losses were low — https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/international/2026/04/02/864470.htm
constraints.breaks_under: abundant reinsurance capacity and low recent claims experience push underwriting discipline aside in favour of volume growth

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Founding members of the Net-Zero Insurance Alliance (2021) pledged to transition underwriting portfolios to net zero by 2050 and to restrict new fossil-fuel underwriting.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: NZIA lost most members within two years (Munich Re, Zurich, Hannover Re, Swiss Re all exited by April 2023 citing antitrust exposure); insurers still collect roughly $21.25bn/year underwriting coal, oil and gas, and only a handful have stopped new oil & gas extraction cover outright.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: Climate commitments were performative once they threatened to constrain revenue or invite antitrust liability; genuine constraint is legal, not moral.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: War-risk pricing is presented as neutral, data-driven actuarial assessment of conflict probability (Joint War Committee zone designations).
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Pricing is asymmetric and selectively responsive: Hormuz/Bab-el-Mandeb premiums spiked from ~0.3% to as high as 3% of vessel value in 2026 as the Iran war escalated, and Black Sea premiums surged 250% after ship attacks in late 2025 — but a comparable escalation in Taiwan Strait naval activity (joint China-Russia exercise, SLBM test, law-enforcement operations) 'produced almost no change in insurance pricing at all,' per market analysis calling this 'pricing war at Hormuz and peace at Taiwan.'
stated_vs_revealed.delta: The market is a genuine live conflict-probability signal for theatres with recent kinetic events, but is not yet forward-pricing Taiwan risk — meaning INS_RE's own pricing understates that specific tail risk, likely because the JWC/Lloyd's syndicate base has thinner information edge on PLA intent than on observed Houthi/Russian strikes.

dependencies.type: insured physical cargo and freight flows
sanctions regime that creates/removes insurable counterparty risk

tripwires.if: indicative war-risk premium on a strait exceeds ~3x its pre-crisis baseline (e.g. >1% of hull value on a route quoted <0.3% a quarter earlier)
tripwires.then: shipowners reroute or cancel voyages and transit volume falls 10-20%+ within weeks — the route is functionally closed without a single additional warship

tripwires.if: quarterly major-loss ratio falls well below the reinsurer's own planning assumption for two consecutive quarters (as in Q1 2026: Munich Re losses at 3.5% of net revenue vs 18% planned)
tripwires.then: the following treaty renewal prices soften materially (~5%) regardless of standing geopolitical risk (Iran war ongoing) — capacity and recent-loss experience dominate pricing over forward-looking conflict risk

tripwires.if: a facility-backed war-risk scheme (e.g. Ukraine 'Unity') is withdrawn or expires without renewal
tripwires.then: premiums on that corridor jump toward unsubsidized market levels within one renewal cycle and effective insured capacity drops sharply, since private capacity alone has shown reluctance to re-enter without a backstop

what_would_change_my_mind: A sustained (multi-quarter) repricing of Taiwan Strait war-risk premia toward Hormuz-like multiples would mean the market has started forward-pricing that theatre, materially changing the value of INS_RE pricing as an early-warning instrument for that specific conflict. Also watch for any regulator granting an antitrust exemption for coordinated fossil-fuel underwriting exclusion — would falsify the 'climate pledges are performative under legal constraint' finding.
